h1: The 6 Best Privacy-Focused Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 camera-free robot vacuums from roborock and eufy, scored on navigation without a lens, dock automation and everyday value.
summary: The roborock Q7 M5+ is the best overall: LiDAR with no camera, 10,000Pa suction and a self-empty dock listed for up to seven to nine weeks. The Q10 S5+ is the sensible mid-range alternative. Eufy's Omni C20 and C28 give you a camera-free option from a second brand. The eufy 11S MAX is the plainest hardware here, with no mop at all.
intro: A robot vacuum visits every room you own, so the question of what it can see is fair. The sharpest dividing line in this category is the sensor. Some models carry a camera for object recognition. Others steer with a spinning laser that only measures distance, and a laser cannot capture a picture of your living room. Everything else, from suction numbers to dock features, matters less if privacy is the reason you are shopping.

We reviewed six robots whose listings point to navigation without a camera and ranked them on the Primea framework. Sensor type, base design, cleaning type and price bucket carried the most weight, and every judgement rests on spec sheets and listing details rather than lab results.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, Up to 7-9 Weeks Self-Empty, 10000Pa
products.verdict: LiDAR navigation with no camera, 10,000Pa and a long self-empty interval.
products.description:
The roborock Q7 M5+ puts the privacy argument and the cleaning argument in the same box. It navigates by LiDAR with no camera, pulls with 10,000Pa of suction, mops as well as vacuums and parks on a dock listed for up to 7 to 9 weeks of self-emptying. LiDAR maps distance rather than imagery, so no lens ever sees your rooms.

It ranks first because the dock interval is the longest of the six. The Q10 S5+ matches the 10,000Pa suction and the self-empty base, but lists no comparable interval. The eufy C28 pushes 15,000 Pa higher, though it sits in the same $200 to $500 bracket.

Buy it for a busy household that wants a hands-off, camera-free robot. The caveat is obstacle handling. Without a camera it cannot tell a sock from a cable, so clear the floor first.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: The same camera-free LiDAR approach with a self-empty base, for under $300.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ mirrors much of the leader. It uses LiDAR with no camera, 10,000Pa suction and a self-empty base, and mops after it vacuums. It lands under $300, within the $200 to $500 bracket, so it is the easiest roborock to justify when budget matters.

It ranks second because the listing gives no self-empty interval, whereas the Q7 M5+ promises up to 7 to 9 weeks. That figure matters for a family that does not want to touch the dock. Against the Q7 L5 below it, you gain the self-empty base, which the cheaper robot lacks.

Choose it for an apartment or mid-size home that wants a camera-free robot with a bin that empties itself. The caveat is the missing interval, so expect to check the dock rather than ignore it for weeks.
products.skipIf: You want the longest empty window.

products.name: eufy Omni C20 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo for Hardwood and Carpet
products.verdict: LiDAR without a camera, a self-empty base and hardwood and carpet capability.
products.description:
The Omni C20 is the eufy to buy if you prefer that brand's app. It uses LiDAR with no camera, mops and vacuums, handles hardwood and carpet, and empties itself at the base. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It ranks third because the listing gives no suction figure, while the roborock Q7 M5+ and Q10 S5+ both list 10,000Pa. Without that number you are trusting the brand rather than the spec. Compared with the C28 below, you give up a stated suction figure and the roller mop, but you keep the same camera-free LiDAR approach.

Buy it for a mixed-floor home where hardwood and carpet share a level. The caveat is the missing suction figure, so check the listing before assuming it matches a 10,000Pa roborock on carpet.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer the eufy brand.

products.name: eufy C28 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 15,000 Pa, HydroJet Roller Mop
products.verdict: The highest suction here, 15,000 Pa, with a roller mop and no camera.
products.description:
The eufy C28 is the high suction option. It lists 15,000 Pa, a HydroJet roller mop, a self-empty base and LiDAR navigation with no camera. A roller mop keeps pressure on the floor and scrubs rather than drags a damp pad, which matters for dried spills.

It ranks fourth, not higher, because suction on paper matters less than dock endurance for most buyers. The Q7 M5+ lists up to 7 to 9 weeks of self-emptying, while the C28 gives no interval. It also sits in the same $200 to $500 bracket as the cheaper roborock models, so the extra suction is the reason to choose it.

Choose it for pet hair, carpet or sticky kitchen floors. The caveat is that big suction numbers do not guarantee navigation skill, and the camera-free design still means you must clear cables.
products.idealFor: Large pet homes wanting camera-free cleaning.

products.name: roborock Q7 L5 Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 8,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: LiDAR mapping and a mop for under $150.
products.description:
The Q7 L5 is the budget route into camera-free navigation. It uses LiDAR with no camera, lists 8,000Pa suction, mops, and builds maps through the app. It lands in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks fifth because it has no self-empty dock listed, so you carry the bin to the trash yourself. That is the main difference from the Q7 M5+, which lists up to 7 to 9 weeks between empties. Suction is also lower, at 8,000Pa against 10,000Pa on its siblings. For a small home on a tight budget, those compromises are reasonable.

Buy it for a small apartment where weekly emptying is no chore. The caveat is the missing dock, plus app-based mapping that still ties the robot to the cloud.
products.idealFor: Small homes on a strict budget.

products.name: eufy 11S MAX Robot Vacuum Cleaner, Super Thin, Quiet
products.verdict: A thin, quiet, vacuum-only robot with no camera and no mop tank.
products.description:
The eufy 11S MAX is the plainest robot here. It is vacuum only, with no mop, a super-thin body and quiet operation, and it lists no camera. Less hardware means fewer features to configure, which is a privacy point of its own.

It ranks last because it does less than anything above it. There is no mop and no self-empty base, and suction is not stated in our facts. The super-thin body helps it slide under low furniture, but it will not rival the 10,000Pa roborock models on thick carpet. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Buy it for hard floors, bedrooms and small spaces where a quiet vacuum is enough. The caveat is that simplicity: if you want a mop or a dock, move up to the Q7 L5 or Q10 S5+.
products.idealFor: Small homes wanting minimal connected hardware.
products.skipIf: You want mapping or a dock.

whatMatters.detail: LiDAR is a spinning laser that measures distance and builds a floor plan. It cannot take a picture, which is why it matters for privacy. Camera robots use a lens to recognise objects and can in principle capture images. Look for LiDAR in the specs and the words no camera, as listed for every roborock and eufy robot here.

Even a robot with no lens connects to an app that stores your floor plan and schedule. That data lives with the maker's cloud. Read the privacy page, turn off optional sharing and use a strong account password. If you want no cloud link, pick a model such as the eufy 11S MAX that can be run from its own controls.

Without a camera, a robot cannot tell a sock from a cable, so it will bump into both and sometimes tangle. This is the trade-off for privacy. Pick up floor clutter before each run and keep cords off the ground. Expect to rescue the robot occasionally, and avoid running it unsupervised in a room full of wires.

Even a camera-free robot is a Wi-Fi device. Putting it on a guest network keeps it away from your computers and phones. Check your router settings for a guest option and give the robot that network only. Avoid linking it to voice assistants unless you need them, because every link adds another data path.

A self-empty base cuts how often you carry the bin around, so it makes a camera-free robot practical for busy households. The roborock Q7 M5+ lists up to 7 to 9 weeks between empties. It is a convenience feature rather than a privacy one. Check the listing for a stated interval, not just self-empty.

faq.q: Does a robot vacuum without a camera still use Wi-Fi?
faq.a: Usually yes, for the app. LiDAR models like the roborock Q10 S5+ have no lens but still connect to a cloud service for maps and schedules, so read the maker's privacy page and decide what sharing to switch off.
It only measures distance, so it cannot capture an image. It does store a floor plan in the app, so protect your account, as you would with the roborock Q7 M5+ or any eufy model here.

faq.q: Is the roborock Q7 M5+ worth more than the Q7 L5?
faq.a: If you want a dock and a long interval, yes: the Q7 M5+ lists up to 7 to 9 weeks of self-emptying and 10,000Pa. For a small home on a tight budget, the Q7 L5 does the camera-free job.

faq.q: Will a camera-free robot avoid cables?
faq.a: Not reliably. Without a camera it cannot identify cords, socks or pet waste, so pick them up first. This applies to all six robots, from the eufy C28 to the 11S MAX, so tidy the floor before every run.

faq.q: Can I use a robot vacuum on a guest network?
faq.a: Usually yes. Put it on the guest Wi-Fi if your router offers one. That keeps a roborock or eufy robot away from your computers while still letting the app work.

faq.q: Which is simplest in terms of connected features?
faq.a: The eufy 11S MAX, a plain vacuum with no mop and no camera. It has fewer features to configure than the mop-and-dock robots, though it lacks the self-empty base of the Q7 M5+, so you empty the bin yourself.

finalTake: Buy the roborock Q7 M5+ if you want the most complete camera-free robot. The Q10 S5+ is the alternative when the dock matters more than the interval. Choose a eufy when you prefer that brand, with the C28 for more suction. Take the 11S MAX for the simplest hardware. Whichever you buy, keep it on a guest network and read the maker's privacy page.
